newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brown says no plans for UK to re-enter ERM.
newsitem.headline: Brown says no plans for UK to re-enter ERM.

text.p: Britain's new Chancellor Gordon Brown said on Monday he had no plans to re-join the Exchange Rate Mechanism but nor did he think two-year membership of the ERM should be a pre-requisite for joining a single currency.
"There has been no change in our position," Brown told a briefing. "We have no plans to re-join the ERM."

Brown, talking to reporters after his debut EU finance ministers meeting in Brussels, was asked if the two-year membership rule as a pre-requisite for EMU membership was cast in stone. He replied simply: "No."
Earlier, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel had said there was no question of waiving the two-year rule for potential EMU entrants.

Brown's comments went a long way to quashing reports last week that Britain was considering re-entering the ERM at a central rate of 2.5 marks. That knocked 10 pfennigs off the pound and the UK currency was still shaky on Monday.
Brown pledged that a planned cut on VAT levied on domestic fuel bills to five percent from eight percent would be in his first budget.
He said EU single market Commissioner Mario Monti had said that he saw "no legal obstacle" to the plan.
Brown said the new Labour government was committed to completing the single market which would mean more British jobs, but he said Britain would retain its veto on taxation policies.
On a day when he was reported to have been warmly received by his EU colleagues, Brown promised a "positive and constructive" approach to Europe.
